Domanivka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaiv Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Domanivka was the site of one of the largest Nazi-Romanian massacre operations documented in this collection: after the August 1941 occupation, a camp was established here holding local Jews who had not been evacuated, alongside Jews from Kryvyi Ozero and Peschanka in Vinnytsia region, and thousands more from Transnistria, including 160 Jews from Kishinev. Thousands of Jews from Odesa were deported to this camp in 1942. Estimates of the death toll vary widely by source, from 20,000 to 52,000 people murdered here. A monument honoring the victims was erected in 1994. Domanivka's Jewish population had been 903 (79 percent) in 1897, operating five Jewish kolkhozes by 1930.
